new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is not phonemic and falls on the last syllable of the word, without exception according to the OPD.
new_statements.exceptions: None ('always'). The OPD separately notes /ii/ and /uu/ are geminate/double vowels rather than long vowels, and minor dialect differences between Sou village and the rest of Kurti (no stress difference mentioned). Caveat from primary data: Blust's 1975 Kuruti field transcriptions (RB2-011 p.320) carry acute marks on the penult in several disyllabic numerals (řúweh, tóloh, háhuw, límweh, ónoh) alongside final marks elsewhere (saŋát, sεdέ?, pohón, paréy), so the 'always final' claim is not independently corroborated.
new_statements.domain_note: Domain stated as 'the word'; OPD examples are citation forms including inflected verbs with subject prefixes (e.g. am.pa.har '2s+be careful'); no discussion of phrase-level prominence or clitics.
new_statements.identity_note: The OPD describes 'Kurti (Ndrukul) [KTM]', Ndramalmal area, Manus Province, villages Sou, Lomwei, Derimbat, Liap, Mundrau, Patlok, Wamandra, Mundripudeu, Pundru = Glottolog kurt1250 (alt. names Kuruti, Ndrugul). Text sample and checking done with speakers around Liap/Ndrompuhnuu; OPD notes minor dialect differences for Sou village. Blust's 1975 'Kuruti' packet is from Liap speakers, same variety. Do not confuse with Kele (kele1258) or Ere, closely related East Manus neighbours whose stress is described by Ross 2002.
